The `match_id` of the completed match replaces the OTP and the eKYC credential fields: the gateway validates the match against its own record and fills the workstation, agent and match-log references from it, so a caller cannot claim a capture happened on hardware it does not own, or for a subject it did not capture.

The match must have reached the `matched` state, must still be inside its 600 second freshness window, and is single-use: once an authorization has been minted from it, reuse is refused. The `patient_id` sent here must equal the `health_id` the match was captured against.

post.description:
Sets the effective coverage for a visit: the POMSF cover that the resulting claim or preauthorization is billed against.

Use it when a household has more than one POMSF cover available to the patient - for example a child who could be billed under either parent's principal cover, or a spouse who is a POMSF principal in her own right and could also be billed under her husband's cover. Call it after the eligibility check and before you bill.

The response echoes back the selection that was applied.

**POMSF covers only.** This endpoint does not apply to general SHA or UHC covers.

**Related documentation:** [Set Coverage](/docs/claims/process/billing/setCoverage), [POMSF Balance](/docs/claims/process/eligibility/pomsfBalance)

oneOf.description: Authorization request for a minor whose consent was attested by a fingerprint match captured through the minors biometrics endpoints. The `match_id` of the completed match replaces the OTP and the eKYC credential fields: the gateway validates the match against its own record and fills the workstation, agent and match-log references from it, so a caller cannot claim a capture happened on hardware it does not own, or for a subject it did not capture.

The match must have reached the `matched` state, must still be inside its 600 second freshness window, and is single-use: once an authorization has been minted from it, reuse is refused. The `patient_id` sent here must equal the `health_id` the match was captured against.

Submits a virtual claim. This endpoint serves outpatient and emergency claims. Inpatient claims are
dispatched through `POST /claims/discharge` instead.

The request body takes one of four shapes:

- **Standard Claim** - an ordinary outpatient claim for an identified patient. The visit end is
  authorised either by OTP (`otp`) or by biometrics (`discharge_auth_guid`), which are alternative
  paths: supply one, not both.
- **Emergency - Identified Patient** - an emergency claim for a patient who has been identified. The
  visit-end authorisation fields are not read for emergency claims. The precondition is doctor consent
  instead: the claim's doctor consent status must be `APPROVED` or the submission is rejected.
- **Emergency - Unidentified Patient** - as above, plus a mandatory `reason_for_unknown_patient`.
- **Finalise a Partial Discharge** - the second call that submits a claim previously discharged with
  `discharge_status: PARTIAL`. It needs only `consent_token` and `discharge_status: FULL`.

`discharge_status` defaults to `FULL`, which discharges the patient and submits the claim in one call,
so omitting it behaves exactly as before.

auth_type.description: How the HIE authenticates to your endpoint. **Required.** `none` is the only value you can set yourself; every other value also requires `secret_ref`, and secrets are stored by the HIE out of band.

base_url.description: Scheme and host the operation `path` is appended to. **Required**, and must be an absolute URL.

entity_type.description: Which entity's status changes this endpoint receives. **Required**, and must be one of the three values listed. A facility holds at most one endpoint per entity type, so register a separate endpoint for each kind you want.

facility_fr_code.description: Facility Registry code this endpoint serves. Used as the fallback selector at delivery time when no tenant matches `tenant_code`, and as a lookup key on `GET /tenants/{tenant_id}/endpoints`.

headers.description: Static headers sent on every delivery to this endpoint. Use them for routing or tracing values, never for credentials.

name.description: Your label for the endpoint. **Required.** It is not parsed and does not have to be unique.

retry_config.description: Retry policy for deliveries to this endpoint. Omit it to accept the platform default.

backoff_ms.description: Delay before the first retry, in milliseconds.

backoff_multiplier.description: Factor the delay is multiplied by after each failed attempt. With `backoff_ms: 1000` and a multiplier of `2`, retries are spaced 1s, 2s, 4s.

max_retries.description: Number of retries after the initial attempt.

secret_ref.description: Reference to the credential the HIE uses for this endpoint. **Required whenever `auth_type` is not `none`.** The HIE issues the value; there is no API route that stores a secret.

tenant_code.description: Selector matched first at delivery time against the `tenant_code` the EDI backend publishes. This is normally the same value as your client ID, and it is unique to you. Defaults to the resolved tenant's own code when omitted, which is usually what you want.

timeout_ms.description: How long the HIE waits for your response before treating the attempt as failed. Defaults to `60000`.

get.description:
Lists the operations registered under an endpoint, optionally narrowed to one `action`.

An endpoint holds at most one operation per action, so filtering by `action=status_changed` returns at most
one result.

**Only active operations are returned**, so a paused operation is absent rather than shown as inactive. Read
it directly by its `operation_id` to see it.

On this `GET` the `tenant_id` segment is genuinely ignored - the handler never reads it - so any non-empty
value works. Unlike the `POST`, nothing is written.

**Related documentation:** [Manage callback endpoints](/docs/claims/process/callbacks/manageCallbackEndpoints)

post.description:
Registers what the HIE does on an endpoint. This is the second of the two calls that set up status
callbacks, and nothing is delivered until it succeeds.

Send `action: status_changed`. The same action serves all three entity types - the parent endpoint's
`entity_type` is what tells a claim integration from a preauth or authorization one.

The operation is attached using `endpoint_id` alone. The `tenant_id` segment is **not** resolved as a tenant
here: it is written into the endpoint's `facility_fr_code` if that column is still empty, so send the
facility's FR code rather than a placeholder.

Supply `path`, or `path_url_override` to send this one callback to an absolute URL that ignores the
endpoint's `base_url`.

**Related documentation:** [Register a callback operation](/docs/claims/process/callbacks/registerCallbackOperation)

parameters.description: **This segment is not a tenant lookup.** On this `POST` it is used to backfill the parent endpoint's `facility_fr_code` when that column is empty, so send the **facility FR code**. Do not send a placeholder such as `_`: it would be stored as the facility code and break delivery's fallback selector. If you set `facility_fr_code` when you created the endpoint, this value is ignored.
